overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the July 6 notice was adequate and posted in time, and the Board's approval of April 13 minutes within four meetings was timely.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to post notice of its July 6 meeting at least 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Town Clerk posted notice of the meeting on June 16.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the July 6 meeting notice, a public hearing on a site plan review, did not include all elements required by the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notice included all of the required elements under the Open Meeting Law, including the date, time, and place of the meeting as well as the listing of the sole anticipated topic.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to approve its April 13 meeting minutes in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board's efforts to approve the minutes within four meetings was appropriate and complied with the law's timeliness requirement.
